---
title: "Tools"
---

RafikiArdhi builds methods for problems where standard tools fall short, and releases them where agreements allow. The free tools below handle common tasks. The advanced versions use continuous, physics-consistent functions and are available through a project or licence.

## Free tools

::: {.cards}
::: {.card-item}
### phySpline: profile harmonisation
Converts soil profiles sampled at any depths to standard depth intervals (for example GlobalSoilMap 0–5, 5–15, 15–30 cm) with a physics-informed spline, so profiles from different surveys can be compared and mapped together.

[rafikisol on GitHub →](https://github.com/rafikisol)
:::

::: {.card-item}
### Carbon stocks
Soil organic carbon stocks for many profiles at once, from carbon concentration, bulk density, coarse fragments and layer thickness, summed over the depth you choose.

*Online version coming soon.*
:::
:::

## Advanced tools

These are RafikiArdhi's in-house tools, applied in projects or licensed on request. [Contact us](contact.qmd) to discuss your data.

::: {.cards}
::: {.card-item}
### holoSpline
Depth functions that harmonise continuous properties and ordered classes, with an uncertainty estimate at every depth. Profiles can be evaluated at any depth, not only at standard intervals.
:::

::: {.card-item}
### Integrated carbon stocks
Stocks integrated over each continuous profile rather than summed layer by layer. Discrete summation can substantially overestimate stocks; integration removes that bias.
:::

::: {.card-item}
### Depth-aware mapping in Google Earth Engine
The physics-informed spline running pixel by pixel in Earth Engine, so maps carry a continuous profile and can be read at any depth or integrated over the whole profile.
:::

::: {.card-item}
### 2D soil-water flux across hillslopes
Steady-state, variably saturated flow across a catena of soil patches, fitted to sensor data. Returns head, water content and fluxes anywhere on the transect, with checks against continuity and Darcy's law.
:::

::: {.card-item}
### Sensor-to-head preparation
Calibrates water-retention parameters per layer, converts sensor water content to pressure and total head, and estimates how much head error is simply sensor noise.
:::

::: {.card-item}
### Analytical map updating
Updates an existing soil map with newer data through a closed-form, process-constrained model, and reports how much information each update adds, so knowledge accumulates rather than being replaced.
:::
:::
